newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar plunges to T$27.775 on stock tumble.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar plunges to T$27.775 on stock tumble.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar plunged against its U.S. counterpart in late trade on Monday, as funds that were pulled out of the stock market during the morning's big tumble flowed out of the Taiwan market, dealers said.
With 30 minutes remaining at 0730 GMT, the local unit had sunk to T$27.775 to the U.S. dollar against Saturday's T$27.660 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$299.5 million.

Taiwan's stock market, beset by political jitters ahead of a planned cabinet reshuffle on Wednesday, plunged by 3.72 percent or 307.55 points on Monday to close at 7,966.64, the index's lowest level since March 25.
"The stock market plunge prompted many investors to withdraw their funds and invest them elsewhere, like in Hong Kong where the market is hot," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
"The political jitters have more direct impact on the stock market than the forex market, but the indirect impact is the same," she added.
Dealers said the central bank was allowing the local dollar to fall as a lower exchange rate would have the effect of boosting Taiwan's exports.
Taiwan in April posted a trade deficit of US$203.5 million, with exports dropping 2.5 percent to US$9.84 billion compared to April 1996.
The central bank said after a board meeting on Thursday that it would not intervene in the island's foreign exchange market.
